# Synthetic APFS reader structures

Invented project fixtures, generated by `generate.py` with Python 3 standard
library field writes and an independent Fletcher implementation. No source
image, personal data or third-party fixture was copied. Fixture generator and
binary test structures are AGPL-3.0-only project contributions; the vendored
reader retains its upstream MIT license.

Each file is 65,536 bytes. These are limited reader structures, not complete
macOS-mountable filesystems: allocator and extent-reference trees are omitted.

| File | SHA-256 |
| --- | --- |
| basic.apfs | fab44b9ea72d71bbe708fcc07197a2285d3e4ccc55e7b408a19d3373427e5d54 |
| case-sensitive.apfs | af9dffa7fdcb0368ace54d9419ef5525f8c4acb48b11f5a46b710a94c6ca04ef |

Covered: block-zero XID 5 / checkpoint XID 10; volume slots 0 and 2 (slot 2
flagged encrypted); volume OMAP XIDs 5/10/11; plain and hashed directory keys;
a 5000-byte two-extent file, clone sharing private ID 70, an all-hole file,
type-1 decmpfs, a symlink, resident and stream xattrs, snapshot metadata and
negative/nanosecond timestamps. Stored hashes in directory keys are dummy
zeroes; directory/name resolution scans parent/type ranges and does not test
CRC-based hashed-name descent. No password or encrypted ciphertext is present.

Regenerate from repository root:

```text
python vendor/apfs/tests/data/generate.py
just test-apfs
just test --lib apfs
```

Rust tests also mutate copies for tombstones, malformed extent/table/geometry,
8 KiB NXSB checksums and invalid checkpoint UUIDs. Host tests wrap the fixture
in an MBR partition to verify evidence-relative runs and compare live metadata
against a directory snapshot, including cancellation cleanup.
